content: Wikipedia policy strictly prohibits personal attacks in any context. Contributors are expected to focus their comments on the content of articles rather than targeting the individuals who contribute to them. Personal attacks are counterproductive, harm the collaborative environment of Wikipedia, and discourage participation in building a high-quality encyclopedia. What constitutes a personal attack? Debate and disagreement are integral to Wikipedia's culture, as contributors often hold differing views on article content. These contributors may represent opposing communities, each seeking to have their perspectives included. The process of synthesizing these viewpoints into a single, neutral article benefits everyone. All contributors are part of the same larger community—Wikipedia—and accusations of personal attacks without justification are themselves considered a form of personal attack. There is no definitive rule distinguishing personal attacks from constructive discussion, but certain behaviors are unequivocally unacceptable. These include: Use of racial, sexual, homophobic, ageist, religious, political, ethnic, or other discriminatory slurs, including those targeting individuals with disabilities. Dismissing or discrediting someone's views based on their affiliations, regardless of whether those affiliations are mainstream or extreme. Threats of legal action. Threats of violence, including death threats. Threats of vandalism to user pages or talk pages. Actions or threats that expose other Wikipedia editors to political, religious, or other forms of persecution by governments, employers, or other entities. Violations of this nature may result in immediate and extended blocks by administrators. Administrators imposing such sanctions are expected to confidentially notify the Arbitration Committee, explaining their actions and rationale. Insulting or disparaging an editor constitutes a personal attack, regardless of how it is expressed. When in doubt, contributors should comment solely on the article's content without referencing its contributor. The prohibition against personal attacks applies equally to all Wikipedians, including those with a history of disruptive behavior or disciplinary actions. Wikipedia fosters a positive online community where individuals are encouraged to learn from their mistakes and improve. Personal attacks undermine this spirit and hinder the collaborative effort to build an encyclopedia. Responding to personal attacks Initial options In many cases, the best response to an isolated personal attack is no response at all. Wikipedia discussions can be stressful, and editors may occasionally overreact. Additionally, the text-only nature of Wikipedia discussions often fails to convey nuances and emotions, leading to misunderstandings. While personal attacks are not excused by these factors, editors are encouraged to disregard angry or poorly worded comments when reasonable and to remain focused on improving the encyclopedia. If a response is deemed necessary, it should be polite and left on the other user's talk page. Avoid responding on an article's talk page, as this often escalates conflicts. It is also crucial to avoid becoming hostile or confrontational, even when faced with abuse. Customized messages addressing the specific situation are generally better received than templates. When possible, seek compromise or common ground on the underlying content issues rather than engaging in arguments about behavior. Particularly offensive or disruptive attacks, such as physical or legal threats, should not be ignored. Extraordinary situations requiring immediate intervention are rare but can be reported on the administrators' noticeboard. Recurring attacks If personal attacks persist despite reasonable requests to stop, the dispute resolution process should be used. Informal mediation and third-party opinions are often effective in resolving conflicts, especially when personal attacks arise from heated debates over article content. Wikiquette alerts provide a streamlined source of outside opinion. In most cases, issues with personal attacks can be resolved through collaboration and a focus on content, without requiring immediate administrator action. Removal of text There is no official policy on when or whether personal attacks should be removed, though this has been a topic of debate. Removing clear personal attacks from your own user talk page is rarely controversial. On other talk pages, especially when the text is directed at you, removal should generally be limited. However, exceptions exist. The most severe types of personal attacks, such as attempts to reveal nonpublic personal information about Wikipedia editors, go beyond mere insults and should be removed for the benefit of the community and the project. In cases involving sensitive information, a request for oversight may be appropriate. Off-wiki personal attacks Wikipedia cannot regulate behavior in media outside the control of the Wikimedia Foundation. However, personal attacks made off-Wikipedia can cast doubt on whether an editor's on-wiki actions are conducted in good faith. Posting personal attacks or defamation off-Wikipedia is harmful to the community and to the editor's relationship with it, particularly when such attacks involve violations of privacy. These actions may be considered aggravating factors by administrators and are admissible evidence in dispute resolution processes, including Arbitration cases. In some instances, evidence may be submitted privately via email.
